original_title: Chadley Is Back For Final Fantasy 7 Revelation, Whether You Like It Or Not
summary_en: Despite player feedback on his omnipresence in Final Fantasy 7 Rebirth, Chadley is confirmed to return in the next installment, Revelation. Director Naoki Hamaguchi teases a deeper narrative involvement for the AI assistant.
ai_analysis: The return of Chadley in Final Fantasy 7 Revelation, with an expanded story role, addresses player reception while signaling a deliberate narrative choice by the development team.

en.title: Chadley Returns in Final Fantasy 7 Revelation, Director Confirms Expanded Role
en.summary: Despite player feedback on his omnipresence in Final Fantasy 7 Rebirth, Chadley is confirmed to return in the next installment, Revelation. Director Naoki Hamaguchi teases a deeper narrative involvement for the AI assistant.
en.body:
The debate surrounding **Chadley's** role in the **Final Fantasy VII Remake** saga has been a lively one, and it seems players will have to contend with the AI assistant once more in **Final Fantasy 7 Revelation**. Game director **Naoki Hamaguchi** has confirmed that Chadley will not only be present but will also feature more prominently in the main story.

In **Final Fantasy 7 Rebirth**, Chadley became an almost inescapable presence, guiding players through the vast open-world segments and offering valuable Materia and Summons. This ubiquity, while useful for some, led to a common sentiment among players: there was simply too much Chadley. However, Hamaguchi indicated that his role is evolving rather than diminishing.

> "Chadley is actually going to have his own room on the Highwind, that serves as his laboratory. In there, Chadley is doing his own research about the meteor," Hamaguchi stated. He further elaborated that while Chadley's previous role as a field guide has been passed to his AI assistant, **Mai**, in **Revelation**, Chadley himself will be more integrated into the core narrative.

This shift suggests that Chadley's involvement will move beyond side activities and into the central plot, likely tied to the looming threat of the meteor. For those who appreciate the duo's dynamic, Hamaguchi also teased that Chadley and Mai will continue to share "humorous and adorable" moments, hinting that their relationship remains a lighthearted element within the game's overarching drama. The director also noted that Chadley's significance has grown organically since his initial introduction in **Final Fantasy 7 Remake**, where his purpose was primarily to facilitate challenge content for obtaining summons.

## A Contentious Companion
The discourse around Chadley highlights a common challenge in game development: balancing player engagement with narrative pacing. While his function in **Rebirth** was to encourage exploration and provide tangible rewards, his constant commentary and quest-giving could feel intrusive to some. The decision to deepen his narrative purpose in **Revelation** aims to address both fan feedback and the evolving story needs, potentially transforming him from a ubiquitous taskmaster into a more integral character.

## What's Next for the Remake Trilogy
With **Final Fantasy 7 Revelation** slated to conclude the remake trilogy, the expanded role of characters like Chadley is crucial. Details regarding the release window for **Revelation** have not yet been announced, but fans can anticipate further revelations about the world, its characters, and the ultimate fate of the planet as Cloud and his allies face their destiny. The integration of Chadley into the main story suggests that his research and perspective will be vital to understanding and confronting the game's climax.

content_raw: If there's one thing that Final Fantasy 7 Rebirth players can agree on, it's that the game has far too much Chadley in it. While he was a valuable source of Summons in Final Fantasy 7 Remake, in Rebirth, he's an omnipresent voice tied to almost every open-world activity thanks to the "CHAD Module" you're burdened with early in the game. Will the Chad be back in Final Fantasy 7 Revelation ? Unfortunately, yes. Will he have an expanded role in the game's story this time? It sure sounds like it, as game director Naoki Hamaguchi teased that Chadley won't be sitting on the sidelines for the final chapter of the remake trilogy. "Chadley is actually going to have his own room on the Highwind, that serves as his laboratory. In there, Chadley is doing his own research about the meteor," Hamaguchi said to GameSpot, while confirming that Chadley's AI assistant Mai will serve as the game's field guide. "In terms of the role that Chadley had in Rebirth, where he would guide you around the various areas and continents that you see on the world map, that role has been given to Mai in Final Fantasy 7 Revelation. Chadley, in Revelation, he's going to have a slightly different role where we'll see a bit more of him in the main story." For the players who are fans of Chadley and Mai, the duo will still have several "humorous and adorable" moments in the game, and Hamaguchi added that Chadley's role had steadily grown since his introduction in Final Fantasy 7 Remake.  "When we were working on the development of the first installment, [battle director Teruki] Endo brought this idea to me: to battle the various summons in sort of a challenge content for the players. And when we were thinking about how we could make that happen, we looked at Chadley. 'Oh, so this guy is an NPC in the Midgar slums, he gives side quests, and he actually has a with her running commentary--and if you're going to be forced to listen to field notes from someone, she's easily a far better choice than Chadley. Final Fantasy 7 Revelation launches in April 2027 for PC, PS5, Xbox Series X|S, and Switch 2. For more on the game, you can read up on how Hamaguchi was inspired by The Witcher 3 and how snowboarding is making its long-awaited debut in the threequel. Interview conducted by Emma Fyffe.
